parties:
Zafar Ali (Md) ----- Petitioner
Vs
Md. Momtaz Hasan & others ----- Opposite Party
full_judgment:
This Rule is directed at the instance of the plaintiff against the judgment and decree dated 13-7-1993 passed by the Subordinate Judge, Natore, in Title Appeal No. 120 of 1991 allowing the appeal and reversing the judgment and decree dated 26-5-1991 passed in Other Class Suit No. 266 of 1987 by the Additional Assistant Judge, Natore, decreeing the suit for declaration that the transfers are mortgage and are subject to redemption.

2. Petitioner filed the suit for declaration that the two kabala deeds dated 18-3-1981 executed and registered by the plaintiff in favour of defendant opposite party No. 1 transferring the lands of Ka and Kha schedule of the plaint have embraced the nature of usufructuary mortgage and not out and out sale and as such, is subject to redemption. In the same sitting two deeds of agreement were executed in favour of the plaintiff by the defendant No. 1, stipulating therein that the suit land would be reconveyed within 7 years on repayment of the consideration money by the vendor to the vendee. Reconveyance, treating the transfer as usufructuary mortgage, having been refused the suit has been filed.

3. Defendant's case is that the transactions were out and out sale as the condition to reconvey the suit land has not been incorporated in the deeds of sale themselves and the deeds of agreement being separate and different one, the transactions do not come within the ambit of section 95(a) of the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act. So the reliefs claimed for declaration as stated above and also for redemption, giving colour of usufructuary mortgage to the transaction, is not legally available.

4. The only question of law involved is whether the transaction namely, transfer of the suit land on the basis of deeds of sale accompanied by separate unregistered deeds of agreement to reconvey the suit land, effected in the same sitting, constitute the transaction as usufructuary mortgage as contemplated in section 95(a) of the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act after amendment of section 95 of the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act by the President's Orders No. 88 of 1972, 136 of 1972 and 24 of 1973 or whether the transactions are an out and out sale. It has been dealt with in different cases by the High Court Division as well as by the Appellate Division. The appellate Court below in this case on its findings that since the deeds of agreement were unregistered and the recitals to reconvey were not incorporated within the body of the sale deeds, the transactions cannot be called usufructuary mortgage, had dismissed the suit both for declaration and for redemption.

<u>5. Mr. Shahidul Islam, the learned Counsel for the plaintiff petitioner, submits that although in t the case of AIi Ekabbar Faraji vs. Bangladesh represented by the Secretary Ministry of Land Administration and others (26 DLR 304), it was decided by a Division Bench that in a transfer by a registered deed of sale if the document itself does not contain the condition of reconvey the transfer cannot" be said to be usufructuary mortgage and it does not come within the ambit of section 95 of the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act, but the said decision has been over-ruled by the Appellate Division in the case of Bangladesh vs. Haji Abdul Gani and others 32 DLR (AD) 233.</u>

<u>6. In that case the Full Bench of the Appellate Division has considered the meaning and leagl sequence of section 95(a) in terms of amendment made by President's Orders 88 and 136 of 1972 and President's Orders 24 of 1973 and it has been held that the High Court Division was wrong to hold that the transaction was not an usufructuary mortgage only because the deed of reconveyance was a separate one. It isalso found in that decision of 32 DLR (AD) 223 that the transfers of present nature accompanied by separate deeds of agreement to reconvey is a complete usufructuary mortgage for 7 years. This decision has got support as well from the decision in the case of Abu Bakkar vs. Nasir Ahmed 34 DLR (AD) 237, wherein it has been held that the sale accompanied by separate agreement to reconvey is a complete usufructuary mortgage. In para 5 of 34 DLR (AD) 237, it has been held as follows:</u>

<u>"Unless earlier redeemed by repayment of the consideration a mortgagor acquires right to redemption on the expiry of the maximum period of seven years, and if the mortgagee does not voluntarily restore possession of the land to the mortgagor, the latter may file a suit for redemption within a period of 60 years from the date of accrual of his right of redemption. In this case the suit was filed just on the accrual of the right of redemption and as such, it is not barred by limitation."</u>

<u>7. Relying on the aforesaid decision Mr. Shahidul Islam attacked the submissions of Mr. ABM Nurul Islam who relied on, for the defendant, on the decision of 26 DLR as referred above. Mr. Islam also cited the decision in the case of 19 DLR 404 Nuruddin Ahmed Chowdhury vs. Gunnu Meah and others wherein it has been held as follows:</u>

<u>"Kabala and agreement of repurchase (Ekrarnama) executed in the same sitting they form contemporaneous agreements and enforcible in law."</u>

8. There is another decision cited by Mr. Shahidul Islam which is reported in 47 DLR 67 in the case of Abdul Kader and another vs. Abdul Aziz wherein his Lordship sitting in a Single Bench has held as follows:

"An agreement for reconveyance can be specifically enforced and the provision for registration for such agreement as required under section 95(2) of the Act is not applicable. Even an oral agreement proved by sufficient evidence may be specifically enforced by the transferor."

9. In the present case Mr. ABM Nurul Islam for the defendant opposite party submits that since the deeds of agreement is not a registered one, it is not admissible in evidence. The submission has been negatived by the decision in the case of 47 DLR 67 and it is also far different from the provision of section 17(2)(V) of the Registration Act which is as follows:

"Any document not itself creating, declaring, assigning, limiting or extinguishing any right, title or interest of the value of one hundred rupees and upwards to or in immovable property, merely creating a right to obtain another document which will, when executed, create, declare, assign, limit or extinguish any such right, title or interest is not compulsorily registerable. "

10. In the case of AIR 1932 (Mad) P•703 the question of registration for separate agreement has been interpreted in the following language:

"A separate agreemnt for reconveyance does not require registration."

11. I myself cite another decision which is AIR 1926 (Born) 497 a full Bench decision wherein it has been held as follows:

"A document namely, the deed of agreement to retransfer, is not inadmissible for only non-registration."

Their Lordships also have held in that decision that if the transaction is in the nature of mortgage the deed of agreement does not require any registration. "

On the same question of law another decision can be looked into which is AIR 1926 (Born) 479 wherein the same principle has been accepted that the deed of agreement is not compulsorily registerable as required under section 17 of the Registration Act. Another decision which is in 16 BLD (AD) 299, is also relevant on the points involved in this case. I myself also have decided a case on the same point of law as reported in 1995 (BW) Page 135.

12. From the discussions above it is very much clear that transaction in question is a complete usufructuary mortgage for 7 years. The deed of agreement although not registered is admissible in law and as such, was legally accepted by the trial Court. It is on record that the deed of agreement 'was made an exhibit without any objection from the other side and in view of the provision of the decisions as referred above in 34 DLR (AD) 237 the limitation for redemption is 60 years. So from the very simple facts of both the parties in this litigation the findings and decision of the appellate Court below is the result of misconception and misinterpretation of the relevant law in the subject as to section 95(a) of the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act, after having been amended by the aforesaid President's Orders. The decision of the appellate Court below, therefore, is not sustainable in law and it is liable to be set aside. Accordingly, the Rule is made absolute. The judgment and decree of the appellate Court are set aside and those of the trial Court are restored. The suit is decreed. Send down the records to the courts below at once.

No order as to costs.

End.
